phrases.notes: هَذِهِ (demonstrative pronoun 'this', feminine) agrees with شَجَرَة (tree, feminine).

phrases.ar: نَعَمْ ، هَذِهِ أُسْرَةُ الرَّسُولِ ، صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ .
phrases.en: Yes, this is the family of the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.
phrases.notes: أُسْرَةُ الرَّسُولِ is an Iḍāfah structure (Possessive construction: 'family of the Messenger').

phrases.en: Peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.
phrases.notes: Honorific phrase recited whenever the Prophet ﷺ is mentioned.

phrases.en: And this is his mother, Aminah.
phrases.notes: وَالِدَة (mother) is feminine, so it uses the feminine demonstrative pronoun هَذِهِ.

phrases.en: And this is his grandfather, Abdul-Muttalib.
And this is his paternal uncle, Al-Abbas.
And this is his paternal uncle, Hamzah.
phrases.notes: Hamzah (حَمْزَةُ) ends in a Tā' Marbūṭah, so it does not take tanween.

phrases.en: And this is his paternal uncle, Abu Talib.
phrases.notes: أَبُو is one of the Five Nouns (الأسماء الخمسة) and takes a Wāw when in the nominative case.

phrases.en: And this is his paternal aunt, Safiyyah.
And this is his son, Al-Qasim.
And this is his son, Abdullah.
phrases.notes: Another son of the Prophet ﷺ.

phrases.en: And this is his son, Ibrahim.
phrases.notes: إِبْرَاهِيمُ is a non-Arabic (foreign) proper noun and does not take tanween.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Fatimah.
phrases.notes: ابْنَة (daughter) + ـهُ (his). Feminine proper names ending in Tā' Marbūṭah do not take tanween.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Ruqayyah.
phrases.notes: Ruqayyah was married to Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him).

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Zaynab.
phrases.notes: Feminine proper nouns in Arabic generally do not take tanween.

phrases.en: And this is his daughter, Umm Kulthum.
phrases.notes: أُمُّ كُلْثُومٍ is a compound kunyah name ('Mother of Kulthum').
